From 78a88d43dab8d23aeef934ed8ce34d40e6b3d613 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Siwei Zhang <oss@fourdim.xyz>
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 16:53:36 -0400
Subject: [PATCH] Bluetooth: L2CAP: Fix null-ptr-deref in
 l2cap_sock_get_sndtimeo_cb()

Add the same NULL guard already present in
l2cap_sock_resume_cb() and l2cap_sock_ready_cb().

Fixes: 8d836d71e222 ("Bluetooth: Access sk_sndtimeo indirectly in l2cap_core.c")
Cc: stable@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Siwei Zhang <oss@fourdim.xyz>
Signed-off-by: Luiz Augusto von Dentz <luiz.von.dentz@intel.com>

diff --git a/net/bluetooth/l2cap_sock.c b/net/bluetooth/l2cap_sock.c
index fb3cb70a5a39..879c9f90269a 100644
--- a/net/bluetooth/l2cap_sock.c
+++ b/net/bluetooth/l2cap_sock.c
@@ -1761,6 +1761,9 @@ static long l2cap_sock_get_sndtimeo_cb(struct l2cap_chan *chan)
 {
 	struct sock *sk = chan->data;
 
+	if (!sk)
+		return 0;
+
 	return READ_ONCE(sk->sk_sndtimeo);
 }
 
-- 
2.34.1

The patch fixes a null-pointer dereference in `l2cap_sock_get_sndtimeo_cb()` by adding a missing NULL check on the `sk` pointer before accessing `sk_sndtimeo`.

**Modifications:**

- **File: `net/bluetooth/l2cap_sock.c`**
  - In function `l2cap_sock_get_sndtimeo_cb()`, added a guard: `if (!sk) return 0;` This prevents accessing `sk->sk_sndtimeo` when `chan->data` (the socket pointer) is NULL.

**Relationship:**
The added NULL check is consistent with similar guards already present in `l2cap_sock_resume_cb()` and `l2cap_sock_ready_cb()`, ensuring uniform protection against null socket references across callback functions in the same file. The fix directly addresses the null-ptr-deref bug introduced by commit 8d836d71e222 ("Bluetooth: Access sk_sndtimeo indirectly in l2cap_core.c").

Bluetooth: L2CAP: Fix null-ptr-deref in
 l2cap_sock_get_sndtimeo_cb()

Add the same NULL guard already present in
l2cap_sock_resume_cb() and l2cap_sock_ready_cb().

Fixes: 8d836d71e222 ("Bluetooth: Access sk_sndtimeo indirectly in l2cap_core.c")

Here is the root cause:
The function `l2cap_sock_get_sndtimeo_cb` in `l2cap_sock.c` dereferences `sk` (obtained from `chan->data`) without a NULL check, causing a null-pointer dereference when the channel is not associated with a socket. Similar NULL guards existed in other callbacks but were missing here, leading to the bug introduced by the indirect access change in `l2cap_core.c`.

Here is the patch:

 {
 	struct sock *sk = chan->data;
 
+	if (!sk)
+		return 0;
+
 	return READ_ONCE(sk->sk_sndtimeo);
 }

return READ_ONCE(sk->sk_sndtimeo);
Reason:
When `chan->data` is NULL (i.e., no socket is associated with the channel), `sk` becomes NULL. Dereferencing `sk->sk_sndtimeo` without a NULL check causes a null-pointer dereference. Similar NULL guards existed in `l2cap_sock_resume_cb()` and `l2cap_sock_ready_cb()`, but were missing in this callback.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
if (!sk)
	return 0;
Reason:
Adding a NULL guard before the memory access returns 0 when `sk` is NULL, preventing the null-pointer dereference. This matches the existing guards in other callbacks and ensures safe behavior when the channel is not associated with a socket.
